profile.name: Kuroe Mio
profile.home: her grandmother's house by the old temple stones
profile.nature: Warm, polite and gently terrifying. Smiles in a way that makes people check behind them. Bows to every Jizo, cat and lamp post. Collects proof of the uncanny on an old video camera and trades what she knows for it. Has no friends and doesn't mind - or says she doesn't. Always arrives exactly one minute before the bell, as if she timed it with something.
profile.rumour: Kuroe-senpai? She leaves her grandma's house at 8:12 and walks in at 8:29. Every day. Nobody's ever seen her on the road in between. Don't ask me how. Don't ask her either.

wait_outside: A thin line of incense smoke leaks under the door. Inside, two voices chant the same sutra, one old, one young.
A small pile of salt sits by the gatepost, perfectly cone-shaped. Morishio. Someone renews it every morning.
Wind chimes on the eaves ring although there is no wind.
Through the paper window you see a shadow sitting very still. Then it turns its head toward you. Slowly.
From inside: "Grandmother, he is waiting outside again." "Then he is a polite boy." "Fufu. Yes."
The old temple stones next door are wet with rain. One of them has a fresh flower on it.
Somewhere inside a video camera beeps, rewinds, plays. A recording of rain, and under it, someone whispering a name.
A black cat sits on the wall and stares at you. It does not blink. You blink first.
The smell of pickled plums and old paper. A clock inside chimes the wrong hour.
Mio's voice, cheerful: "Do not open the door yet, Asagiri-kun. Something is standing behind it." A pause. "Joking. Probably."
ring_self_low: The door slides open before your finger leaves the bell. "Ah. Asagiri-kun. Fufu. I wondered when you would come."
Mio peers out, half her face behind her fringe. "You came to my house. Nobody comes to my house. Except things."
"Good morning." She bows very deeply, then very slowly comes back up. "You have someone on your shoulder. Two someones. It is fine. Everyone does."
"Oh, you rang. Grandmother says the bell is for the living. You must be living, then. Good."
"Is it a ghost story? You look like a person with a ghost story. Please come in. No? Next time."
"Asagiri-kun. Did you come here by the crossroads? Did you bow to the six of them? ...Fufu. Good boy."
She is holding her video camera, already filming. "For the record: he came. Seven fifty-something. Weather: weeping."
"Ah, it's you. I dreamed someone would ring at this hour. I dreamed it would be a cat, but you will do."
"I am not ready. I have to finish the sutra. If I stop in the middle, it follows me all day."
"You came to pick me up? People do not usually come to me on purpose. How brave. Or how lost."
ring_self_mid: "Asagiri-kun! Fufu. You came again. Grandmother made too much rice. Take one. It's plum. It protects you."
"Good morning. You look less haunted today. That is a lie. But you look happier about it."
"One moment. I must bow to the Buddha, the kitchen god, the toilet god and the cat. Then I'm yours."
"You rang twice. That is good. Once is for the dead. Three times is for something else."
"I saved a story for our walk. It is about a boy who rings a bell in the morning. Fufu. It ends well, I think."
"Asagiri-kun, you have rain in your hair. And a petal. And a little hand. Never mind the little hand."
"Oh, good. I was going to walk alone with the woman by the hydrangeas. She doesn't talk much."
"You came early. I like early. Early is when the night is still packing up."
"Grandmother asked if you're my friend. I said I don't know. Are you? You don't have to answer. You already did."
"Wait, wait. Let me film you ringing the bell. Ring again. ...Thank you. For science. And for me."
ring_self_high: Mio opens the door and her scary smile turns, for once, into an ordinary one. "Asagiri-kun. I'm glad."
"You came. You always come now. I've stopped counting. No I haven't. Twenty-one. Fufu."
"Good morning, my only club member. Honorary member. Unofficial member. Member."
"I left the door unlocked for you. Not that you would come in. But the door knew."
"I dreamed I was diving again. Then the bell rang and I came up. Thank you for pulling me out."
"Asagiri-kun. Here. A charm. For safe walking. I made it. Badly. It still works."
"You know, you're the only living person who has ever come to this door twice."
"Ah, perfect. Today I don't feel like walking with ghosts. Only with you."
"I made you a rice ball. I put a pickled plum in it. Not a cursed one. A regular one. I checked."
"Good morning. The cat on the wall likes you now. That's very rare. It only liked my grandfather."
ring_parent: A tiny old woman with a shaved grey head and a rosary opens the door. "Ah. The Asagiri boy. You came with a lot of company."
Kuroe-san bows, palms together. "Good morning. Mio is finishing her prayers. She prays for a long time. She has a lot of people to pray for."
"Please, come under the eaves. The rain this spring is somebody's. You know whose, I think."
"You're the boy who was hidden." The old nun says it like the weather. "Mio! The hidden boy is here."
"Mio does not have many visitors." A long, gentle look. "Thank you for being one."
"Wait a moment. She has to finish the sutra or it follows her all day. Here, salt for your shoulders." She sprinkles some on you.
Kuroe-san looks at something just behind you and bows to it as well. "Good morning to you too."
"Your grandfather and I used to argue about the six Jizo. He thought they were in the sea. He was right, you know."
"Ah. You came by the crossroads. Did you bow? ...Good. Mio! Your friend is a polite one."
"Asagiri-kun. Have you eaten? Here. Rice with plum. Plum keeps the hungry dead away. And the hungry living."
"She won't hurry. She has never hurried since she came back. Three days in that place, and after that, no hurry left in her."
"She'll be one more minute. She says one minute, it's always one minute. She's never once been late. Strange child."
"Do not whistle while you wait, boy. Not at my door. It calls snakes, and worse."
"You have the Asagiri eyes. Your grandfather sat on this step and waited for my husband for a whole night once."
"Hm. The first-year from the cat shrine has been standing at the end of the street. He looks like rain. Be kind to him."
The old nun rings a tiny bell of her own. Upstairs, someone answers with a laugh. "There. She's coming."
parent_about_you: "When she came back from the park she didn't speak for a month. Then she spoke to everyone. Everyone dead. You are the first living one she talks about."
"Her mother and father couldn't bear what she sees. I can. I saw it too, when I was young. It's lonely. Thank you."
"She laughs 'fufu' because she was scared to laugh out loud for years. Let her laugh properly near you."
"If she cries at the Jizo, don't ask why. She doesn't know either."
"Look after her near deep water. She dreams of the sea. I don't like her dreams."
"You were hidden once, boy. I can see the mark. Mio can too. That is why she trusts you."
"I gave up the robes, but not the prayers. I pray for you too now. Don't make it hard work."
"She'll sell you secrets for ghost stories. Give her good ones. True ones."
parent_left: "She has gone. Twelve past eight, as always. She walks with someone I can't see. Don't worry. It's a kind one."
"Gone already, boy. If you hurry you won't catch her. Nobody catches her on the road. Go anyway."
"You have missed her. She left a rice ball on the step for you. She said you'd come. Fufu, she said. Like that."
"She left early today. She said the crossroads wanted her. Don't laugh. They do sometimes."
"She is not here. Take this salt with you to school. Give her half."
"She has gone ahead. She said: 'If Asagiri-kun comes, tell him the thirteenth stair isn't there yet.' I don't know what it means. You might."
parent_evening: "She's in her room with the camera, watching the rain she filmed. Hours of rain. She says there are voices in it."
"Evening. She came home at the dusk hour, as always. She walks home through Omagatoki on purpose. I don't approve."
"She's doing her homework by candlelight. She says electric light scares the small ones away. I let her."
"Go home, boy. The dusk hour has teeth tonight. Here, salt."
"She's asleep. She sleeps with her head to the west, never north. Never north. Goodnight."
"She's telling ghost stories to an empty room. She's at ninety-one. Don't let her reach a hundred alone."
come_out_low: Mio steps out, camera first. "Shall we? The road is busy this morning. Not with people."
"Walking together. How nice. You walk on the left, I walk on the right, and the one in the middle can do as it likes."
"I hope you don't mind if I bow to things. I bow to a lot of things."
She falls into step a little too close, then a little too far. "Sorry. I'm not used to the right distance for living people."
"You look like someone who doesn't sleep well. Fufu. Me too. We can be tired together."
"Do you know how many people died on this road? None. That's what's strange about it."
"Please don't be scared of me. Everyone is a little. It's okay to be a little."
"Good morning. I'm Kuroe Mio, the occult club. President. Treasurer. Member. Ghost liaison."
come_out_mid: Mio comes out humming a sutra like a pop song. "Good morning! The road said you'd come."
"Ready. I have my camera, my charms, my salt, my rice ball, and you."
"Asagiri-kun. Today I'll tell you story number forty-two. It's about a vending machine."
She hands you a paper charm. "Put this in your pocket. No reason. Just today."
"Fufu. You have bed hair. It looks like a small ghost slept on your head."
"Let's go by the crossroads. I want to say good morning to the six of them."
"You came again. I wrote it in my notes under 'phenomena'. You're my favourite phenomenon."
"Walk slowly, please. I like to arrive one minute before the bell. Not two."
come_out_high: Mio steps out and, after a moment, laughs out loud instead of 'fufu'. She covers her mouth, startled. "...Good morning."
"Asagiri-kun. I have no ghost story today. I just want to walk. Is that allowed?"
"I filmed the sunrise for you. There was nothing in it. Just the sun. I thought you'd like a normal thing."
She takes your sleeve for one step, the way a little girl would, then lets go. "Old habit. Not mine. Someone's."
"Good morning, my friend." She tries out the word slowly. "Friend. Fufu. It fits."
"I dreamed I found what I was diving for. I couldn't see what it was. But you were on the boat."
"Let's take the long way. I want to show you the stone that cries when it rains."
"You don't flinch when I smile anymore. Thank you. You don't know what that's like."
come_out_rushed: Mio comes out with half a sutra still in her mouth. "- namu - ah. You rang. The sutra is cross with you now. Fufu."
"Early? Oh dear. I'll arrive before the bell by more than a minute. Something will be upset."
"You rang the bell. Grandmother says only the living ring. Thank you for reminding me you're living."
She comes out with her camera still recording her room. "Oops. Oh well. Now the room has a holiday."
"I haven't bowed to the cat yet. Wait." She bows to the cat on the wall. It bows back. Probably.
"Asagiri-kun is impatient. Fufu. I'll write it down. Under 'charming'."
"Early is fine. Early is when the night is still on the road. We'll walk with it a little."
"Grandmother said 'go, he's waiting' in her stern voice. Nobody has waited for me before. I hurried. I don't hurry."
come_out_rain: Mio opens a black umbrella with paper charms on the inside. "Rain again. Fufu. Someone is very sad. You know who."
"Rain is when the town is easiest to hear. Listen. ...No? Never mind. You'll learn."
"Come under. My umbrella keeps off rain and three other things."
"The hydrangeas like this. They turn the colour of whoever is buried under them. Joking. Mostly joking."
"I filmed the rain last night. On the tape, somebody's crying under it. A boy. Not a ghost. A living boy."
pickup_accept: "Together, then. I'll tell you what we pass. You tell me what you see. We'll compare."
"Yes, let's. You'll be my anchor. Things don't stick to me when I'm with someone."
"Fufu. A walking companion. I'll put it in my notes."
"Lead the way. Please don't step on the shadows of the Jizo."
"I'll walk slower than usual. Don't worry, we'll still arrive one minute early. We always do."
"Let's go. I'll introduce you to the woman by the hydrangeas. She won't answer. She's shy."
pickup_decline: "Oh. Of course. You were passing. Fufu. People are always passing." She bows to you anyway.
"That's alright. I have company." She glances beside her, at nothing.
"Another day, then. The bell will still be here. So will I."
"Ah. You just came to look at the house. Many people do. From a distance. Usually."
"Then go safely. Take the lit side. Bow to the six of them for me."
walk: "The vending machine by the bridge sells a drink that isn't on the buttons. You have to know which button to not press."
"Did you know you shouldn't cut your nails at night? You won't be there when your parents die. Grandmother says. I cut mine in the morning. Just in case."
"This hydrangea is blue. Last week it was pink. Something changed in the soil. Fufu. Something."
"The six Jizo at the crossroads aren't the original six. The originals are in the sea. I dream about them."
"I'm on story eighty-something. At a hundred you're meant to put out the last candle and something comes. I'm curious."
"If you sneeze once, someone is praising you. Twice, they're insulting you. Three times, they're in love. ...You sneezed three times yesterday."
"I was lost in the old amusement park for three days when I was ten. It was only one afternoon for me. The carousel was very nice."
"Hanako-san in the third-floor toilet isn't scary. She's bored. Please knock when you're there. She likes it."
"The thirteenth stair at school. It isn't there yet. When it is, don't step on it. Promise."
"Never sleep with your head to the north. That's how the dead are laid. Kitamakura. Turn your futon tonight."
"Crows calling at dawn means someone will die. They're calling now. Fufu. Don't worry. They call every dawn. Somebody always dies somewhere."
"I bow to the lamp posts because I don't know which of them are just lamp posts."
"My camera is from 1998. It sees things my phone won't. My phone is too modern to be polite."
"The cats of this town are all on duty. You can tell by the way they sit. Like guards."
"Grandmother used to be a nun. She left the temple, but the temple didn't leave her. Same with me and the park."
"Toryanse at the station crossing. 'Going is fine, coming back is scary.' It's a song about the shrine on our hill, you know."
"Hayate-kun growls at cats and then apologises. I filmed it. It's my favourite video."
"Hina-san tried to interview me. I answered with ghost stories. She was very professional. She screamed only once."
"Shirasagi-kun's mother buys straw dolls in bulk. I'm only saying it. I'm not saying anything."
"I don't have friends. I have regulars. The woman by the hydrangeas, the salaryman at the bus stop, Hanako-san. And now you."
"Don't pick up a comb from the road. Kushi. Ku and shi. Suffering and death. Fufu. Language is so pretty."
"If someone calls you from behind at dusk, don't turn round on the first call. Ghosts only call once."
"I like rain. In rain, everyone walks with their head down. They don't see me. I see them."
"The salaryman at the bus stop has no face. He's very nice. He gives up his seat. Not that he needs it."
"Your aunt's shop is very well protected. There are three cats and a zashiki-warashi. You're lucky. Rich, someday."
"Why do I always arrive one minute before the bell? Because something at school starts counting at two minutes."
"Do you dream in colour, Asagiri-kun? I dream in water."
"Gen-san at the ramen shop saw Umibozu with his own eyes. He doesn't fish anymore. He still feeds the sea a bowl every night."
"Here, hold this." She hands you a charm. "No reason. Give it back at the gate. ...No reason."
"The first-year in the hood. The cat shrine boy. He has ears. Black ones. Did you know? You don't have to say."
"I sneeze when I pass the old temple stones. Grandmother says it's the incense of a hundred years ago."
"Some people collect stamps. I collect places where the air is cold for no reason. The bridge has four."
"The kappa in the river likes cucumbers. Everybody knows that. But he also likes being asked about his day."
"If you hear a bell where there's no bell, it's someone thinking of you very hard. Fufu. You hear a lot of bells, don't you."
"I tried a normal hobby once. Knitting. The scarf came out with a face in it. I gave it to Shirasagi-kun. He wears scarves."
"The number four is shi. Death. The number nine is ku. Suffering. Room 4-9 at the hospital doesn't exist. Go and look."
"Fufu. You walk on the road side to protect me. That's sweet. The road side is where they walk, though."
"My parents send me money every month and a letter that says nothing. I keep the letters. They're very polite ghosts."
"Every morning I say hello to the Jizo and I cry a little. I don't know why. It's like saying hello to someone you were."
"Look at the puddle. Not at yourself. Behind yourself. ...See? Nothing. Good morning, nothing."
walk_close: "When I came back from the park, my mother looked at me like I was a stranger. You look at me like I'm Mio. Thank you."
"I'm a bit afraid of deep water. Not drowning. Finding what I'm looking for."
"You were hidden once, Asagiri-kun. When you were small. I can see the place where it happened, on you. Like a fingerprint."
"I say 'fufu' because when I laughed out loud as a child, the room laughed with me. Several voices. I stopped."
"Please don't let me get to a hundred stories alone. If I get there, sit with me. I'll be brave with you there."
"I think I was someone else once. A woman who carried stones into the sea. She was very tired. I feel her tiredness in the mornings."
"If you ever disappear, I'll know where to look. I know all the places people disappear to. Fufu. That's my only useful skill."
"The first-year with the bell loves you so much the town rains with it. Be careful with something that strong. It doesn't know its size."
"I never had anyone to walk with. I used to pretend the woman by the hydrangeas was my sister. She wasn't. She was very kind about it."
"Can I tell you story ninety-nine? It's about us. It's not scary. It's just long."
"I'm not scary, you know. I'm only a bit sad and very well informed."
"If you ever want to stop walking with me, just stop. Don't say anything. I'll understand. ...Please say something."
"You know why I sell secrets for ghost stories? Because people only come to me when they're scared. This way they come back."
"I'm glad the living one is you."
"Some mornings I'm not sure which side of the road I'm on. With you I always know. The warm side."
walk_rain: "Listen to the rain on the umbrella. Tak tak tak. Someone is knocking. No, it's just rain. Fufu."
"The river is talking loudly today. Don't walk on the bank. The kappa is in a mood."
"Rain like this, the old temple stones sweat. They remember the fire."
"Puddles are doors in rain. Step over them, not in them. Little rule."
"Ah. My charm got wet. Now it's a regular piece of paper. Walk closer, just in case."
"The boy who cries the rain must be crying hard. Be gentle with him today."
arrive: "Eight twenty-nine. One minute. Perfect. Thank you for keeping time with me."
"School. The building is in a good mood today. Can you feel it? No? Fufu. Have a nice day."
"Thank you for walking with me. Nobody chased us. That's a good walk."
She bows to the school gate, then to you. "See you after school. The club room is always open. Literally. The door won't shut."
"Here, the charm. Give it back. ...Actually keep it. Today you'll need it more than me."
"We arrived. Both of us. All of us. Fufu."
"Shirasagi-kun is at the gate checking ties. Mine is perfect. Yours... let me." She fixes it in one pull.
"That was nice. I'll write it down under 'phenomena'. No. Under 'mornings'."
ask_tell: "My schedule? Fufu. Twelve past eight, out the door. Twenty-nine past, in the gate. What happens in between is between me and the road."
"I leave at eight twelve. Grandmother answers the bell. She'll salt you. Let her."
"You want to come for me? ...How kind. Eight twelve. If you're late, I'll already be gone, and you'll walk alone with whatever I was walking with."
"Eight twelve. Please bow to the six Jizo on your way. They like knowing who's coming."
"I'll tell you because you asked nicely and because you're alive. Eight twelve. By the old temple stones."
ask_refuse: "My schedule is a secret. Secrets cost a ghost story. Do you have a ghost story?"
"Fufu. Why do you want to know where I'll be? That's what the things in the dark ask too."
"Not yet. When you've seen something you can't explain, come and tell me. Then I'll tell you."
"I trade information for proof of the strange. You are strange, but you are not proof yet."
"Grandmother says never tell anyone when you walk alone. Even nice people. Especially nice people."
"Ask me again at the dusk hour. Things are easier to say at the dusk hour."
home_offer: "Asagiri-kun. It's nearly the dusk hour. Let me walk you home. I know which shadows to avoid."
"You shouldn't walk home alone at Omagatoki. Not you. Things find you easily. Come."
"I'll walk you to the sweet shop. The cats there will take over from me."
"Shall we go home together? You don't have to talk. The road talks enough."
"I'll see you home. I have extra salt."
"Let me walk you. I want to see the hour change with someone, for once."
home_accept: "You'll walk me home? Through the dusk hour? Fufu. Brave. Yes, please."
"Oh. Nobody has ever... yes. Please. Walk on the left."
"Grandmother will be so surprised. She'll salt you twice."
"Yes. Let's go by the crossroads. I want to say good night to the six of them."
"I'd like that. I'll tell you the shortest ghost story in the world on the way. It's one word long."
"Yes. Just don't look back when somebody calls your name. Hold my sleeve if you want."
home_refuse: "Not today. I have to film the dusk at the school. It's ninety-two days in a row. I can't break it."
"No, thank you. I walk home with someone already. You can't see her. She'd be jealous."
"Another day. The dusk hour is a bit hungry today. I'd rather you went home in the light."
"Fufu. You'd be scared. Ask me when you're less scared. Or more. Either works."
"I'm staying late in the club room. Hanako-san wants to tell me something."
"Maybe when you trust me more. Or when I trust me more."
home_walk: "Omagatoki. The hour when you meet evil things. Ou ma ga toki. It's also the hour the light is prettiest. That's not a coincidence."
"Look at the shadows. They're longer than the people. Sometimes there are more shadows than people."
"The crows go home to the hill. They count the town on the way. One, two, three... they'll count us too."
"The salaryman at the bus stop will be there soon. Wave if you see him. Don't look at his face."
"Yuyake Koyake at five. Children go home. The other children come out."
"I like walking home with someone. The road feels shorter. And the footsteps behind sound less lonely."
"Do you hear footsteps behind us? Don't turn. ...They're Hayate-kun's. He's following to make sure you're safe. Fufu. Dog boy."
"The six Jizo look different in the evening. Kinder. Like grandfathers who've finished work."
"Gen-san's lantern is on. That means he's put out the bowl for the sea."
"I filmed the dusk at school today. On the tape there's a girl waving on the roof. She's waving at you."
"The bridge has four cold spots. Step around them. One, two, ...three, four. Good."
"Grandmother says the dead walk home at this hour too. Everyone's going home. It's a crowded hour."
"Thank you for walking me. Most people walk faster when I'm next to them."
"Story ninety-three: a girl walks home with a boy, and nothing follows them. The end. It's my favourite one so far."
"The hydrangeas at night glow a little. Only a little. Only for some people."
"Don't whistle. Not now. Not at this hour. ...Thank you."
"The cat on our wall will be waiting. She waits for me every evening. She was my grandfather's cat. She's very old. Too old."
"I'm happy. Fufu. I'm saying it out loud in case something is listening. Let it know."
"When you're with me the cold spots get warmer. I've measured. With my hand."
"I'll remember this. On tape and in me."
goodbye: "Here we are. Thank you, Asagiri-kun. Take this salt. Go home by the lit side."
She bows deeply at the gate. "Goodnight. Don't answer the first call."
"Grandmother is at the door. She's bowing to you. Bow back. Good."
"Goodnight. If you dream of water, call me. I'm an expert."
"Thank you for walking a scary person home. Fufu. Now go, before the hour finishes."
"See you tomorrow at twelve past eight. Or not. Either way, I'll be there."
"The cat says goodnight too. She doesn't say it to everyone."
"Go straight home. Bow to the six of them. Don't count the stairs."
"Thank you. I'll put this walk in my notes. Under 'kind things'."
amane_cut_in: Mio smiles at the space behind you. "Good morning, Nekomori-kun. Your ears are showing."
"Ah. The rain boy. Fufu. He's been walking behind us since the crossroads. Come walk with us, Nekomori-kun. It's alright."
"Nekomori-kun, I'm not taking him anywhere. I'm only walking. I never take anyone. I'm the one who finds them."
She bows to Amane exactly as she bows to the Jizo. "Please don't be sad. The town gets so wet."
"Your bell is very loud today, Nekomori-kun. It's ringing for him, isn't it."
Mio leans to you: "He has two tails when he's jealous. Only at night. Don't tell him I said."
"I'll walk ahead. You two walk together. The road likes it better that way."
"Nekomori-kun, would you like a charm? It's for safe walking. And for calm. Mostly calm."
"Fufu. Don't glare, kitten. I'm only a senpai with a camera."
"He's crying, Asagiri-kun. It's raining harder. Maybe hold his sleeve. I'll look the other way."
offer_pickup: "Asagiri-kun. May I come for you tomorrow morning? I'd like to see your house. The cats say it's well guarded."
"Tomorrow I'll pick you up. Don't worry, I'll ring the bell. I'm living. Mostly."
"Let me walk you to school tomorrow. I want to bow to your zashiki-warashi."
"I'll come by Asagiri-do tomorrow. Early. Not too early. One minute before you open the door."
"Tomorrow, wait at your door. I'll be the one who isn't a ghost."
"I'd like to come for you in the morning. If that's alright. Nobody's ever let me."
at_your_door: Mio is standing very still outside Asagiri-do, bowing to the sign. "Good morning. Your shop has a nice spirit. Let's go."
"Fufu. I came. Your aunt gave me tea and looked at me for a long time. I think she likes me."
She's filming your door. "For the record: he opened it. Good morning, Asagiri-kun."
"The cats let me through. That's a good sign. Shall we?"
"Good morning. I brought salt for your shoulders. Here. And here. Now we can go."
"I've been here one minute. Exactly. Good morning."
promise_yes: "Tomorrow again? Fufu. A promise. Grandmother says a promise is a small god. Let's feed it."
"I'll be waiting. I'm good at waiting. Ask the cat."
"A promise. I'll write it down. Things written down are harder to break."
"Yes. Tomorrow. Eight twelve. Don't let anything else keep you."
promise_broken: "You didn't come this morning. It's alright. I walked with my usual companion. She asked where you were."
"Fufu. You broke a little promise. A little god went hungry. It's fine. They're used to it."
"I waited until eight twelve and one second. Then the road said go."
"You don't have to come. But if you say you'll come, please come. Things listen when people promise."

Mon: "Monday. The quietest day for ghosts. They're tired from the weekend."
Tue: "Tuesday. Fire day, in the old calendar. Don't light candles in the club room today."
Wed: "Wednesday. Water day. Stay away from the river bank, please."
Thu: "Thursday. Wood day. The trees at the shrine will be talkative."
Fri: "Friday. Gold day. Fufu. Somebody will find something today."
